## 🎯 Context and Goal
<!-- What problem should be solved, for whom, and why? Include representative
     use cases, examples, evidence, or relevant links where they clarify the need. -->

## 🔍 Proposed Behavior
<!-- Describe what users or callers should observe. Include examples, important
     errors or edge cases, and any changes to public APIs, configuration, or
     externally visible data. Avoid prescribing internal implementation details. -->

## 📐 Domain Language
<!-- Define new or changed domain terms introduced by this proposal. State each
     concept's precise meaning and, where relevant, its identity, lifecycle,
     relationships, or invariants. Note renamed or superseded terms.

     Describe domain concepts, not proposed classes, interfaces, database tables,
     or fields. Use these terms consistently throughout the rest of the proposal.
     Write "None" if the domain language is unchanged. -->

| Term or concept | Definition | Change |
|-----------------|------------|--------|
|                 |            | New / changed / superseded |

## ✅ Scope and Constraints

### In scope
<!-- Capabilities and externally observable changes included in the proposal. -->

### Out of scope
<!-- Plausible adjacent capabilities deliberately excluded. -->

### Constraints
<!-- Requirements every acceptable implementation must preserve, such as
     compatibility, security, privacy, performance, platform, or dependency
     constraints. Omit if there are none. -->

## 🔀 High-Level Approach
<!-- Describe the design decisions needed to prevent incompatible
     interpretations, without breaking the work into implementation tasks.
     Mention material alternatives, trade-offs, or dependency decisions only
     when they help explain or constrain the chosen approach. -->

## ❓ Open Questions
<!-- List unresolved decisions and mark anything that blocks implementation.
     Before implementation begins, blocking questions should be resolved or
     moved into the proposal as explicit decisions. Write "None" if resolved. -->

- None.

## 🏁 Acceptance and Validation

### Feature acceptance
<!-- Add feature-specific, externally observable outcomes that establish when
     the proposal has been implemented correctly. -->

- [ ]

### Baseline completion checks
<!-- This is a starting checklist, not an exhaustive Definition of Done.
     Extend it with any additional checks required by this feature. -->

- [ ] New behavior and important failure cases are tested.
- [ ] The repository's full validation command passes.
- [ ] Affected public documentation is updated.
